Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Serre obtained the p-adic limit of the integral Fourier coefficient of modular forms on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ for $p=2,3,5,7$. In this paper, we extend the result of Serre to weakly holomorphic modular forms of half integral weight on $\Gamma_{0}(4N)$ for $N=1,2,4$. A proof is based on linear relations among Fourier coefficients of modular forms of half integral weight. As applications we obtain congruences of Borcherds exponents, congruences of quotient of Eisentein series and congruences of values of $L$-functions at a certain point are also studied. Furthermore, the congruences of the Fourier coefficients of Siegel modular forms on Maass Space are obtained using Ikeda lifting.

Serre proved that, for the primes \(p=2,3,5,7\), the integral Fourier coefficients of modular forms on \(SL_{2}(\mathbb{Z})\) admit a \(p\)-adic limiting behavior. His result has played an important role in the study of congruences between modular forms and in the \(p\)-adic theory of modular forms.

The present paper extends Serre’s theorem to a broader setting. Specifically, it considers weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight on the congruence subgroups \(\Gamma_{0}(4N)\), where \(N=1,2,4\). In this context, the Fourier expansions may have poles at the cusps, but the paper shows that their coefficients still satisfy \(p\)-adic limiting properties analogous to those established by Serre in the integral-weight case.

A key ingredient in the proof is the use of linear relations among Fourier coefficients of modular forms of half-integral weight. These relations make it possible to control the coefficients of weakly holomorphic forms and to compare them with coefficients of holomorphic modular forms. Through this approach, the paper establishes the desired \(p\)-adic convergence and congruence properties.

Several applications are derived from the main theorem. These include congruences for Borcherds exponents, which arise in infinite product expansions associated with Borcherds lifts. The paper also obtains congruences involving quotients of Eisenstein series and investigates consequences for special values of \(L\)-functions at certain points. These results demonstrate that the \(p\)-adic behavior of half-integral weight modular forms has implications across several areas of the theory of automorphic forms.

Finally, the paper applies these ideas to Siegel modular forms. Using Ikeda lifting, congruences for Fourier coefficients of Siegel modular forms in the Maass Space are obtained. This connects the half-integral weight theory developed in the paper with higher-degree Siegel modular forms, showing that the extended form of Serre’s \(p\)-adic congruence phenomenon has further consequences in the theory of lifts and special subspaces of Siegel modular forms.

The paper generalizes Serre’s theorem on \(p\)-adic limits of Fourier coefficients of modular forms with integral weight to the setting of weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight. More precisely, it studies modular forms on \(\Gamma_0(4N)\) for \(N=1,2,4\), where the Fourier expansions may have poles at the cusps, and proves that their Fourier coefficients satisfy \(p\)-adic limiting properties analogous to those established by Serre in the integral-weight case.

The central method is based on explicit linear relations among Fourier coefficients of weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight. These relations make it possible to transfer \(p\)-adic information between coefficients and to control their behavior modulo increasing powers of a prime \(p\). In this way, the paper shows that many coefficient sequences arising naturally in half-integral weight modular forms exhibit systematic \(p\)-adic congruence phenomena.

Several applications are developed from this general framework. One application concerns Borcherds products: the exponents appearing in infinite product expansions associated with Borcherds lifts satisfy congruences that follow from the half-integral weight theory. Another application treats quotients of Eisenstein series, where the resulting Fourier coefficients can be analyzed \(p\)-adically using the same coefficient relations. The paper also connects these congruences to special values of \(L\)-functions, showing that certain arithmetic quantities arising from special \(L\)-values inherit related \(p\)-adic properties.

Finally, the results are applied to Fourier coefficients of Siegel modular forms lying in the Maass Space. Through Ikeda lifting, modular forms of half-integral weight are linked to Siegel modular forms, and the \(p\)-adic congruences obtained in the half-integral weight setting can therefore be translated into congruence results for Fourier coefficients of these higher-degree automorphic forms.

Overall, the paper broadens the scope of Serre-type \(p\)-adic limit theorems from integral-weight modular forms to weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight. It also demonstrates that the resulting congruence phenomena extend beyond classical modular forms, influencing Borcherds products, Eisenstein series, special \(L\)-values, and Siegel modular forms arising from lifting constructions.
outputs.L5:
Jean-Pierre Serre, Fourier analysis, and Richard Borcherds are connected through deep areas of modern number theory, especially modular forms and automorphic forms.

Serre’s work had a major influence on arithmetic geometry and the theory of modular forms. His ideas helped shape the modern understanding of Galois representations, congruences between modular forms, and the relationship between algebraic structures and analytic objects. One of his famous contributions, Serre’s modularity conjecture, became a central guiding problem in number theory and was later proved by Khare and Wintenberger.

Fourier expansions play a fundamental role in this subject. A modular form is often studied through its Fourier series, usually written as

\[
f(q)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n q^n,
\]

where \(q=e^{2\pi i z}\). The coefficients \(a_n\) contain rich arithmetic information. For example, they may encode divisor sums, point counts on elliptic curves, or data related to Galois representations. Serre emphasized the importance of these coefficients and their congruence properties, showing how analytic expressions can reveal hidden arithmetic patterns.

Richard Borcherds extended the theory in a striking direction. His work on automorphic forms and infinite-dimensional Lie algebras led to the theory of Borcherds products. These are automorphic forms expressed as infinite products, often constructed from Fourier coefficients of modular forms. Borcherds used such ideas in his celebrated proof of the monstrous moonshine conjecture, which connects modular functions with the representation theory of the Monster group.

Together, Serre, Fourier expansions, and Borcherds products illustrate a central theme of modern mathematics: the same object can be viewed through analysis, algebra, geometry, and number theory. Fourier coefficients provide the language, Serre’s ideas reveal arithmetic structure, and Borcherds’ constructions show how these structures can lead to unexpected and beautiful connections.

We extend Serre’s \(p\)-adic limit theorem for Fourier coefficients of modular forms to the setting of weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight on \(\Gamma_0(4N)\).  More precisely, for suitable primes \(p\) and weakly holomorphic forms
\[
f(\tau)=\sum_{n\gg -\infty} a_f(n)q^n
\]
of weight \(\lambda+\tfrac12\), we establish \(p\)-adic limiting congruences for the coefficients \(a_f(n)\), showing that certain normalized coefficient sequences tend \(p\)-adically to coefficients of holomorphic modular forms or to explicitly described \(p\)-adic modular forms.  The argument combines half-integral weight trace formulas, congruences for \(U\)- and \(V\)-operators, and a careful analysis of the principal parts at the cusps of \(\Gamma_0(4N)\).

As applications, we obtain \(p\)-adic information on several arithmetic quantities naturally governed by half-integral weight modular forms.  First, we derive congruences and limiting formulas for Borcherds product exponents arising from weakly holomorphic input forms.  Second, we apply the theorem to quotients of Eisenstein series, giving \(p\)-adic convergence results for their Fourier coefficients.  Third, using the relationship between half-integral weight coefficients and central values of \(L\)-functions, we obtain congruences for families of algebraic \(L\)-values.  Finally, via the Ikeda lifting, we transfer these \(p\)-adic limit phenomena to Fourier coefficients of Siegel modular forms.  These results provide a half-integral weight analogue of Serre’s theorem and exhibit a common \(p\)-adic framework linking weakly holomorphic modular forms, automorphic products, special \(L\)-values, and higher-degree Siegel modular forms.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a research article about extending Serre’s results on p-adic limits of Fourier coefficients for \(SL_2(\mathbb{Z})\) and \(p=2,3,5,7\) to half-integral weight modular forms on \(\Gamma_0(4N)\), \(N=1,2,4\).
counterfactuals.output:
The article extends Jean-Pierre Serre’s classical work on \(p\)-adic limits of Fourier coefficients of modular forms for \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\) to certain spaces of **half-integral weight weakly holomorphic modular forms**.

## Background

Serre studied how Fourier coefficients of modular forms behave \(p\)-adically, especially for the small primes

\[
p=2,3,5,7.
\]

For modular forms of integral weight on \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\), he showed that certain sequences of Fourier coefficients have strong \(p\)-adic convergence properties. Roughly speaking, coefficients of modular forms of level \(1\) often tend to \(0\) \(p\)-adically after applying suitable \(p\)-power operations.

The article asks whether analogous phenomena occur for **half-integral weight modular forms**, which live naturally on congruence subgroups such as

\[
\Gamma_0(4N).
\]

The cases considered are

\[
N=1,2,4,
\]

so the levels are \(4,8,16\).

## Main setting

The paper studies weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight

\[
k=s+\frac12
\]

on \(\Gamma_0(4N)\), with \(N=1,2,4\). These forms are allowed to have poles at cusps, usually at the cusp \(\infty\).

A central role is played by canonical bases of such spaces. These bases generalize the Duke–Jenkins bases for integral weight weakly holomorphic modular forms. A typical basis element is denoted something like

\[
f_{k,m}^{(4N)}(z)
=
q^{-m}+\sum_n a_k^{(4N)}(m,n)q^n,
\qquad q=e^{2\pi iz}.
\]

The coefficients

\[
a_k^{(4N)}(m,n)
\]

are the main objects of study.

Because the weight is half-integral, the Fourier exponents are restricted by congruence conditions modulo \(4\), connected to Kohnen’s plus-space condition. Thus one only sees indices \(n\) lying in certain square-class congruence classes.

## Goal of the article

The article’s goal is to prove that, for primes

\[
p=2,3,5,7,
\]

the Fourier coefficients of these half-integral weight basis elements satisfy \(p\)-adic limiting behavior analogous to Serre’s classical results.

In broad terms, the paper studies limits of the form

\[
a_k^{(4N)}(m p^r,n)
\]

or related expressions as

\[
r\to \infty,
\]

and proves that under suitable hypotheses these coefficients converge \(p\)-adically, often to \(0\).

Equivalently, the \(p\)-adic valuations of these coefficients tend to infinity in many cases.

## Main results

The paper proves that Serre-type \(p\)-adic convergence holds for half-integral weight forms on

\[
\Gamma_0(4),\quad \Gamma_0(8),\quad \Gamma_0(16).
\]

More concretely, for the canonical basis coefficients

\[
a_k^{(4N)}(m,n),
\]

the authors establish congruences and divisibility estimates showing that sequences such as

\[
a_k^{(4N)}(m p^r,n)
\]

become increasingly divisible by powers of \(p\) as \(r\) increases.

Thus, for suitable \(m,n,k,N\),

\[
a_k^{(4N)}(m p^r,n)\longrightarrow 0
\]

in the \(p\)-adic topology.

The primes \(2,3,5,7\) are special because they are exactly the primes for which Serre’s original level-one results have particularly strong forms. The article shows that the same small-prime phenomenon persists in the half-integral weight setting, despite the additional complications coming from half-integral weights and higher level.

## Methods

The paper combines several tools from the theory of modular forms.

### 1. Canonical bases

The authors construct or use explicit bases for spaces of weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight on \(\Gamma_0(4N)\). These bases make it possible to track Fourier coefficients precisely.

### 2. Zagier duality

A key structural feature is a duality between Fourier coefficients of basis elements in complementary weights. This is a half-integral weight analogue of Zagier duality.

It relates coefficients such as

\[
a_k^{(4N)}(m,n)
\]

to coefficients in another weight, typically \(2-k\) or a related dual weight.

This duality allows the authors to transfer divisibility information between different weights.

### 3. Hecke-type operators

The proof uses operators such as \(U_p\) and \(V_p\), which act on Fourier expansions by

\[
\left(\sum a(n)q^n\right)\big|U_p
=
\sum a(pn)q^n
\]

and

\[
\left(\sum a(n)q^n\right)\big|V_p
=
\sum a(n)q^{pn}.
\]

These operators are essential for studying what happens to coefficients when indices are multiplied by powers of \(p\).

### 4. Cusp behavior and genus-zero structure

The levels \(4,8,16\) are small and have favorable modular curve structure. This allows the authors to control poles and cusps explicitly. Such control is necessary because the forms considered are weakly holomorphic, so one must carefully track possible principal parts at cusps.

### 5. \(p\)-adic valuation estimates

The heart of the argument is to prove lower bounds for

\[
v_p\!\left(a_k^{(4N)}(m p^r,n)\right),
\]

where \(v_p\) is the \(p\)-adic valuation. Showing that these valuations grow with \(r\) proves \(p\)-adic convergence to zero.

## Significance

The article shows that Serre’s \(p\)-adic philosophy is not limited to integral weight modular forms on \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\). It extends naturally to half-integral weight forms of levels \(4,8,16\).

This is important because half-integral weight modular forms are closely connected to:

- theta functions,
- quadratic forms,
- partition-type generating functions,
- Shimura correspondences,
- traces of singular moduli,
- mock modular forms and harmonic Maass forms.

The results therefore provide new \(p\)-adic information in settings where half-integral weight forms naturally arise.

## Overall summary

The article proves that the Fourier coefficients of canonical basis elements for half-integral weight weakly holomorphic modular forms on

\[
\Gamma_0(4N),\qquad N=1,2,4,
\]

satisfy Serre-type \(p\)-adic limiting properties for the primes

\[
p=2,3,5,7.
\]

Using canonical bases, coefficient dualities, modular operators, and careful cusp analysis, the authors show that many sequences of coefficients become increasingly divisible by powers of \(p\), and hence converge \(p\)-adically, often to zero. The work extends Serre’s classical level-one integral weight results to a half-integral weight setting and demonstrates that the same small-prime \(p\)-adic phenomena persist at levels \(4,8,16\).

counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.**  
We prove a half-integral weight analogue of Serre’s theorem on the \(p\)-adic limiting behavior of integral Fourier coefficients of modular forms. More precisely, for weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight with algebraic integral Fourier coefficients, we establish congruence and limiting results describing the \(p\)-adic distribution of their coefficients along suitable arithmetic progressions. The proof combines the theory of weakly holomorphic forms on congruence subgroups, \(p\)-adic modular forms, and the arithmetic of the half-integral weight Hecke action, together with a careful analysis of principal parts at the cusps.

As applications, we obtain \(p\)-adic congruences for Fourier coefficients of half-integral weight Eisenstein series and derive corresponding congruences for arithmetic invariants encoded by these coefficients. In particular, via the known relations between Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series and special values of Dirichlet and quadratic-twist \(L\)-functions, our results yield new \(p\)-adic limiting formulas and congruences for special \(L\)-values. We further apply these congruences to the Fourier coefficients of Ikeda lifts, whose coefficients are governed by products of local factors and special \(L\)-values, obtaining \(p\)-adic continuity and vanishing results in families of Fourier coefficients. These results extend Serre’s integral-weight \(p\)-adic framework to the weakly holomorphic half-integral setting and provide new tools for studying congruences among automorphic forms and their associated arithmetic invariants.

counterfactuals.output:
We establish congruences for Fourier coefficients of modular forms of half-integral weight on \(\Gamma_0(4N)\), with nebentypus character, in a setting suitable for arithmetic applications.  Using a refinement of the \(q\)-expansion principle together with half-integral weight Hecke operators and explicit filtration arguments, we prove that congruences modulo powers of primes between half-integral weight forms are detected by finitely many initial Fourier coefficients.  The resulting criteria are uniform in the level and character and are compatible with the Kohnen plus space when \(N\) is odd.

As applications, we obtain congruence theorems for the exponents occurring in Borcherds products attached to weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight.  In particular, we give effective conditions under which two Borcherds products have exponents congruent modulo a prescribed prime power, and we relate these congruences to congruences among their input forms.  We further apply the main theorem to quotients of Eisenstein series, proving families of congruences for their Fourier coefficients after suitable normalization.  Finally, by means of the Borcherds lift and the Fourier–Jacobi expansion, we derive congruences for certain Siegel modular forms arising from automorphic products.

These results provide a unified framework for transferring coefficient congruences from half-integral weight modular forms to arithmetic invariants encoded in infinite products and higher genus modular forms.  They also yield effective bounds, making the congruence conditions computationally verifiable.
